summary: Iteration 25: full backend + admin/customer UI verification of coupon PUBLIC/PRIVATE visibility and server-side coupon analytics. Created pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_coupon_analytics_iter25.py (39 tests) covering create/default/update visibility, available-list filtering + view-event logging, private validate (eligible + ineligible: min-order, first-order-only, category), first-order visibility for a brand-new customer (registered + deleted), analytics for all date ranges + custom, per-coupon stats (public & private), usage history against real existing redeemed orders, admin-auth security on analytics/stats/usage, redemption counts not inflatable via repeated validate calls, and regression (delivery coupon, expiry, invalid code, bulk generate with visibility, /api/coupons). 39/39 passed. Admin UI: dashboard cards, all 5 filters, private badge, mini stats, create-with-visibility dialog, stats page (funnel/metrics/usage table/range buttons/back) all verified, including a coupon with real redemptions (SAVE10: 2 rows, ₹300 discount, ₹8,787 revenue). Customer UI: private coupon absent from Available Coupons modal (12 public listed), public apply/remove works, private code applies via manual entry (-₹25), invalid code shows error. All test coupons, test users, test coupon_events and the temporarily added cart item were cleaned up.

minor.issue: totals.first_time_users is computed as unique_customers - repeat_users, i.e. it means 'customers who used the coupon exactly once', not 'customers on their first order'. Verified on SAVE10 (1 customer, 2 orders) -> first_time_users=0, repeat_users=1. UI label 'First-time users' is therefore misleading; either rename to 'Single-use customers' or derive from _is_first_time/order history.

usage_limit=0 (and usage_limit_per_customer=0) is falsy in _assert_eligible/available_coupons, so a 0 limit is silently treated as unlimited instead of blocking. Validate returned 200 for a usage_limit=0 coupon.

One 'view' event is inserted per visible coupon on every call (12 inserts per checkout page load, and the checkout page calls it repeatedly), and db.coupon_events has no index on code/created_at while analytics/stats do full-collection scans in Python. Views inflate quickly and will degrade. Suggest de-duplicating views per user/day and adding indexes on (code, created_at).
Iterates every non-cancelled coupon order and every coupon_event in Python instead of using MongoDB aggregation; fine now but O(all orders) per dashboard load.

issues: React a11y console warning: 'Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}' on both dialogs
Category filter lists all categories including ones no coupon targets, so selecting them yields an empty grid with no 'no coupons match' empty state message

action_items: Rename/redefine stats.totals.first_time_users (currently = single-use customers, not first-order customers) or fix the AdminCouponStats label.
Treat usage_limit == 0 as a real zero limit (use `is not None` checks) in _assert_eligible and available_coupons.
Add indexes on db.coupon_events (code, created_at) and de-duplicate 'view' events per user/coupon/day to stop view inflation from repeated /coupons/available polls.
Add aria-describedby/DialogDescription to the coupon Add/Bulk dialogs to clear the React a11y warning.
Optional: add an empty-state message in the admin coupon grid when filters match no coupons.
critical_code_review_comments: coupons.py is ~640 lines and mixes customer validation, admin CRUD and analytics; consider splitting analytics into routers/coupon_analytics.py.

Analytics correctly derive redemptions/revenue/discount from db.orders (verified: repeated validate calls left redemptions at 0), and private coupons are excluded from /coupons/available while still validating by code — core design is sound.
_customer_name does a per-user find inside the usage loop with a local cache — fine, but a single $in query would be cleaner.
